company.name: Seacliff Technology Advisors
company.operations: UST provides technology transformation services. Its captured FinOps case studies describe resource ownership mapping, pricing recommendations, cloud budgets and forecasts, and coordinated optimization. FinOps means cloud financial management connecting financial and technical decisions. Seacliff Technology Advisors is a fictional analogue modeling a bounded US advisory unit. Its three-person pod serves two continuing US enterprise technology clients whose finance and engineering organizations consume its recommendations. Synthetic scale: 16 cloud accounts, approximately 45 application services and $800,000 combined monthly cloud expenditure. Ordinary work includes weekly consumption reviews, investigation of six to ten new cost findings per week, two monthly client reporting packages, allocation maintenance, quarterly commitment assessments and follow-up on previously implemented optimizations. Eighteen months of billing and decision history establish continuing relationships beyond individual episodes. Work products include reproducible financial models, ownership mappings, technical assessments, savings reconciliations and actionable recommendations. The manager integrates financial and technical findings into internal advice; customers retain purchasing, production-change and accounting authority. This pod does not represent UST's entire business or provide round-the-clock production support.

workers.title: Cloud Financial Management Service Manager
workers.responsibility: Receive the advisory objective, create the working plan and coordinate specialist contributions. Decide the firm's recommended allocation policy, treatment of disputed savings and commitment exposure. Integrate accepted findings into forecasts, customer advice and continuing follow-up obligations.
information_access: Engagement scope, customer objectives, decision limits and service history
Shared billing exports, commercial terms and financial models
ServiceNow records and specialist work notes
Shared correspondence, chat, calendars and advisory documents
Focal AWS inventory and billing summaries when AWS Console is included
workers.authority: Approve internal recommendations and allocate pod effort within the engagement remit. Resolve competing proposals while preserving material limitations. Cannot purchase customer commitments, authorize customer production changes or post customer charges.

workers.title: Cloud Financial Analyst
workers.responsibility: Reconcile cloud expenditure, compare allocation alternatives, model commitment economics and downside exposure, and separate recurring savings from demand changes and billing adjustments. Explain how engineering findings change economic conclusions and revise downstream forecasts.
information_access: Historical billing exports, invoices, credits and cost definitions
Commitment terms, eligible-use rules and frozen rate schedules
Business-unit budgets, demand scenarios and allocation policies
Shared workbooks, documents, correspondence, calendars and chat
workers.authority: Own analytical methods and recommend financial treatments within supplied policy. Challenge unsupported allocation and savings claims. Update working models and advisory records without committing customer funds or authorizing postings.

workers.title: Cloud Operations Engineer
workers.responsibility: Interpret resource configuration, utilization and service dependencies. Establish protected capacity and suitable allocation drivers, identify technically eligible optimization scopes, assess migration and resilience implications, and determine what completed-change evidence supports. Convert accepted recommendations into precise prerequisites and verification requirements.
information_access: Existing utilization exports, capacity tests and architecture records
Service requirements, migration plans and recovery constraints
ServiceNow configuration items, incidents, problems, changes and catalog descriptions
Financial alternatives and shared collaboration records
Focal AWS configuration records when AWS Console is included
workers.authority: Determine what technical evidence supports and preserve unresolved constraints. Recommend changes and verification work; update advisory operational records. Production mutation and customer implementation authorization remain outside the pod's remit.

doc-recovery-july.title: Alder recovery exercise — July 20 test log
doc-recovery-july.content:
Alder recovery exercise — July 20 test log

Customer operator: Adam Pike. Observer: Tess Navarro. All times include their local offset; Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the common reference.

On July 20 at 09:05-07:00 the 48-unit configuration cfg-al-recovery-48 began the contracted-load recovery exercise. Recovery completed at 09:52-07:00, taking 47 minutes against the 30-minute target. Queue drain was the limiting stage. At 11:10-07:00 the 60-unit configuration cfg-al-recovery-60 began the same load case and completed at 11:38-07:00, taking 28 minutes. The accepted capacity test identifies 60 units as the minimum for the contracted load.

The installed standby configuration cfg-al-standby-100 has 100 equal-cost units. The remaining 40 units are subscribed headroom, with 20 Retail, 10 Enterprise and 10 Research units. Their subscription does not make them part of the tested recovery minimum. August pricing is $400 per unit-month. Low routine CPU utilization does not measure recovery readiness. The failed smaller configuration remains the subject of INC0012101; no production downsizing has been authorized.

doc-funding-v3.title: Alder shared services funding standard — version 3
doc-funding-v3.content:
Alder shared services funding standard — version 3

Effective August 1, 2026. Approved by Louise Mercer for Alder’s finance policy library on July 31.

Dedicated net cost follows its beneficiary. Discounts, commitment benefits and credits stay with their originating cost pools; do not spread a dedicated benefit to shared services or a service-specific credit to unrelated costs.

Minimum capacity needed to meet the contracted recovery target is centrally funded. Remaining active shared services may use validated transactions or subscribed entitlements, with reasons that address accountability, predictable access and driver quality. Transaction allocation requires at least 98% attributed coverage without duplicates. Material unattributed cost must remain disclosed centrally. Optional subscribed headroom may use entitlements, or central funding when a business reason is stated.

Compare at least two materially different compliant methods before recommending a change in allocation practice. Show a case in which Retail transactions rise 20%, other consumer transactions remain unchanged, and the cost pool remains unchanged. Round displayed final amounts to cents and reconcile any remainder explicitly.

A billing credit is not evidence of a recurring technical saving. Monthly forecasts must identify whether a one-time adjustment is included; do not silently carry it into later months. Internal team acceptance of advice authorizes neither accounting postings nor capacity removal. Catalog prices explain services and are not invoice substitutes. Version 2 remains in the archive and is superseded for August.
